title_vi: Lưu trữ khối, tệp và đối tượng: khác nhau ở thứ chương trình nhìn thấy

source_snapshot.note: Pinned commit/path body read from a partial clone of the source repository; git hash-object of the retrieved body matches the source-map blob. No source-image bytes used.

related.reason_vi: Các trường hợp dùng kho đối tượng.
Kho đối tượng thường giữ dữ liệu bằng mã xóa.
Tải tệp lớn lên kho đối tượng.

claims.evidence: The Amazon S3 User Guide pages on object keys and folders (2023, last commit with content) and Ceph's Ceph Clients page were read from clones of awsdocs/amazon-s3-userguide and ceph/ceph; the inode and block numbers were measured by the author, who ran mkfs.ext4 and debugfs (e2fsprogs 1.47.0) on a 64 MiB image file on 2026-10-18.

mobile.evidence: Chromium (Playwright) rendered lesson.md (markdown-it, tables enabled, every <details> open, a 16 px page gutter) at each width: the page never scrolled sideways and the figure was scaled to the column; the smallest SVG font-size times that scale is the recorded minimum at 320 px. `python3 -m scripts.figures check --browser` measured every line of the figure in Chromium inside its box. Not GitHub, not a real phone and not learner testing.

claims.claim_vi: The Amazon S3 data model is a flat structure with no hierarchy of sub-buckets or subfolders; hierarchy is inferred from key name prefixes and delimiters; the console shows photos/2017/example.jpg as folder photos containing folder 2017; console folders cannot be renamed (2023 guide, general purpose buckets).
claims.section: Creating object key names; Organizing objects in the Amazon S3 console by using folders
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of awsdocs/amazon-s3-userguide at commit cc53dd6a44d3aa1d654e6d3705a0a7550f20fd2a.

claims.claim_vi: Instead of reading the entire object, a GET can read only a portion of the object data by specifying a byte range.
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of awsdocs/amazon-s3-userguide at commit cc53dd6a44d3aa1d654e6d3705a0a7550f20fd2a.

claims.claim_vi: Ceph clients get block devices (RBD: resizable, thin-provisioned, snapshots and clones, striped across the cluster), object storage with S3- and Swift-compatible APIs (RGW) and a POSIX file system usable with mount or FUSE (CephFS).
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of ceph/ceph at commit c0b32d47115c516baef9eb0111b4dc1c21c91ff4.

claims.claim_vi: Measured: a 64 MiB image formatted ext4 with 4 KiB blocks; /docs/note.txt (28 bytes) written with debugfs got inode 13 and an extent at block 2066; reading block 2066 of the image with dd returned the file's 28 bytes.
claims.verified_by: The author ran and measured this on 2026-10-18 without mounting the image; speed was not measured.

claims.claim_vi: The source states: Three storage categories: block storage presents raw blocks and is owned by a single server, file storage is built on block storage with a directory hierarchy shared over SMB/NFS, object storage stores objects in a flat structure accessed by a RESTful API; examples listed include 'Google block storage'. The lesson does not adopt 'Google block storage' as an object store (see source_deviations).

design_notes_vi: Ba thẻ theo thứ chương trình nhìn thấy, bốn bước thử tìm khối của một tệp, ba giao diện của Ceph. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: The source names 'Google block storage' as an object store; the lesson notes that Google's object service is Google Cloud Storage.
The source calls object storage mainly for cold, archival and backup data; the lesson does not repeat that and shows the three types as interfaces, with Ceph offering all three on one cluster.
editorial_note_vi: Bài mới viết trong kho này, chờ review kỹ thuật. Chưa user testing hoặc phê duyệt phát hành.
